posts.title: Mythic Foundry
posts.blurb: Turning a rough AI-generated concept into a production-ready mark — clean vector redraw, grid and clear-space rules, and a full brand guide with color and type system.

cardThumbs.alt: Mythic Foundry emblem in reversed white, for dark backgrounds
Mythic Foundry wordmark only, no emblem
Logo finalization page comparing the AI-generated reference against the hand-redrawn line art, with grid and clear-space guides

posts.heroAlt: Finished Mythic Foundry emblem — a dragon coiled above a glowing anvil, with the "Mythic Foundry" wordmark below, full color
body: The client came in with an AI-generated concept for a dragon-and-anvil emblem — a strong idea, but unusable as a production logo: rough edges, inconsistent linework, no defined proportions.

The job was to turn that concept into an actual usable mark: redrawing it as clean vector line art, defining clear-space and sizing rules against a strict grid, and building a full system around it — a "forge glow" full-color palette (warm amber, orange, and rust plus near-black and off-white, with exact hex/RGB/CMYK values) alongside a monochrome version for single-color use. Typography pairs BeaufortPro Heavy for the primary wordmark with Platypi Bold as a secondary face.

Deliverables were a complete brand guidelines document — the redrawn emblem in full color and monochrome, a transparent lockup, a small-format/favicon version, and explicit dos-and-don’ts for using the wordmark against different backgrounds.

posts.title: onebynine.ai (1x9 Systems)
posts.blurb: A grounded, people-first mark for an AI operations consultancy — a 3x3 grid icon that spells out "1x9" through its own construction, paired with a clean wordmark system.

cardThumbs.alt: onebynine.ai wordmark lockup
onebynine.ai icon, orange colorway
onebynine.ai reversed white lockup
onebynine.ai icon, black colorway

posts.heroAlt: 3x3 grid icon mark in a green gradient, rounded square, with one cell shown as a white X shape
body: onebynine.ai (internally called 1x9 Systems) is a technical consulting brand focused on operations modernization and practical, AI-driven workflow automation for small and midsize businesses — deliberately not a flashy "AI toys" pitch. The mark needed to hold that grounded, people-first tone rather than looking like a generic tech-startup logo.

The concept is a 3-by-3 grid — nine squares, reading as "1 of 9" / "one by nine" — with one cell replaced by an X shape, so the icon itself spells out the multiplication "1x9" instead of relying on a wordmark trick alone. It works as a standalone favicon-scale glyph or paired with the "onebynine.ai" wordmark as a full lockup. The palette is a rust orange and dark earthy green, chosen specifically to avoid a generic SaaS look.
The finished system covers full-color and reversed lockups, a standalone icon mark in multiple colorways, and a wordmark built to scale from a browser favicon up to a full site header.

posts.title: DeWitt Schools Yard Signs
posts.blurb: Recurring personalized athlete yard signs for DeWitt Public Schools — roughly ten new sport designs a year, thousands of signs printed over the run of the program.
posts.cardAlt: DeWitt Swim and Dive yard sign design

cardThumbs.alt: DeWitt Baseball yard sign
DeWitt Cheer yard sign

posts.heroAlt: DeWitt Swim & Dive yard sign design with a custom swimmer illustration and Panthers mascot
body: While at MMD Signs, DeWitt Public Schools became a recurring client for personalized athlete yard signs — the kind families put in the yard to celebrate a student’s season. Coroplast, 18"x24", built to survive a Michigan season outdoors.

Each sport got its own design: a custom swimmer illustration for swim & dive, a mascot-and-diamond layout for baseball, star-and-paw graphics for cheer, plus versions for football, softball, volleyball, archery, and more, across both the high school and middle school. Every design was templated with a "Student Name" field so the shop could personalize and output them fast, sport by sport, season after season.
This became one of the highest-volume recurring jobs on the floor — roughly ten new designs a year on top of reprints, amounting to thousands of signs printed and sold over the run of the program.

posts.title: Jesus Loves MSU
posts.blurb: An outreach tee for Element Church’s table at MSU’s Sparticipation fair — a play on words up front, the real message on the back.
posts.cardAlt: Jesus Loves MSU t-shirt front design

cardThumbs.alt: Back of the Jesus Loves MSU t-shirt
Shirt worn in person, front design
Shirt worn in person, back design

posts.heroAlt: Dark green t-shirt reading "JESUS LOVES MSU" in green and white lettering
body: Designed while working at Element Church in East Lansing for their presence at Sparticipation 2024, Michigan State University’s annual student-organization fair. The shirt needed a hook strong enough to stop students walking a crowded row of tables — something that read as Spartan gear first and a church shirt second.

The front plays it straight: "Jesus Loves MSU" in Spartan green and white, readable at a glance and impossible not to reread once it lands. The back carries the actual message — "Change the Backyard, Change the World" wrapped around a globe graphic, with the church’s name and site tucked underneath so anyone who liked the shirt actually knew where it came from.
Produced and worn on-site at Sparticipation 2024, doing double duty as event swag and outreach in the same piece of cotton.

posts.title: Michigan State Commander Vehicle
posts.blurb: Official vehicle graphics for the American Legion’s elected Michigan State Commander — flag graphics, military seals, and a veterans-crisis-awareness decal, designed to read as dignified as the role itself.
posts.cardAlt: Ford Explorer with Michigan State Commander vehicle graphics

cardThumbs.alt: Rear flag graphic and seals on the Explorer
Be The One hood decal on the Explorer
Front three-quarter view of the Explorer

posts.heroAlt: White Ford Explorer with American Legion Department of Michigan graphics and "Michigan State Commander" lettering on the door
body: This Ford Explorer is the official vehicle for the American Legion's Michigan State Commander — an elected position — so the graphics needed to read as dignified and official, not like standard fleet branding.

The design pairs the state organization's mark and "Michigan State Commander" title lettering with an American-flag graphic across the rear glass, a star-and-stripe rocker panel treatment, and a clean line of military branch seals along the front fender. A "Be The One" veterans-crisis-awareness decal on the hood ties the vehicle to the Legion's national suicide-prevention campaign.
Fully designed and installed in-house. The wrap now travels with the Commander to American Legion events statewide.

posts.title: American Legion Membership Van
posts.blurb: A full vehicle wrap for the American Legion, Department of Michigan — organizational branding, program logos, and military branch seals, with QR codes built in for on-the-spot membership and donations.
posts.cardAlt: American Legion membership van, full vehicle wrap

cardThumbs.alt: Front of the American Legion van
Rear QR-code panels on the van

posts.heroAlt: White cargo van fully wrapped with American Legion, Department of Michigan branding, military branch seals, and program logos
body: The American Legion, Department of Michigan needed a rolling recruitment and donation vehicle — something that could show up at events, ballgames, and community drives and make the case for membership on sight, not just carry cargo.

Full exterior coverage combines the primary American Legion mark and "Veterans Strengthening America" tagline with sub-program branding — American Legion Baseball, the Legion Riders — plus a full column of military branch seals down the side, laid out to read cleanly at a glance rather than as clutter. Scannable QR codes on the rear windows tie directly to "join" and "donate" actions, turning the van itself into a functional touchpoint instead of a rolling billboard.
Designed and installed personally, start to finish. The van now works as a mobile recruitment tool at Legion events across the state.

posts.kicker: Case Study · Podcast & Broadcast Branding · September 2022
posts.title: Pulpit Aside
posts.blurb: Competition-winning podcast identity for two pastors from different churches — illustrated face-card branding built out into a full broadcast package of lower thirds, title cards, and banners.

cardThumbs.alt: Pulpit Aside video title card
Pulpit Aside broadcast lower thirds
Pulpit Aside YouTube banner
Pulpit Aside simplified banner variant

posts.heroAlt: Square podcast cover art — yellow gradient background with overlapping blue "PULPIT" and orange "ASIDE" text blocks
body: In fall 2022 I entered a branding competition for a new podcast co-hosted by two pastors from different churches, built around a simple premise: set the pulpit aside and compare their church cultures on broader, everyday topics outside the traditional religious bubble. The identity needed to read as progressive and conversational, not churchy.

I benchmarked the top 100 podcasts on Spotify and YouTube and landed between two references: the face-card layout and bold type of Smartless, and the vector-traced character portraits of Pardon My Take. My first pass leaned on an icon combining a microphone, a pulpit, and a cross — conceptually sound but too rigid. I pivoted to illustrated portraits of the two hosts instead, built from reference photos in a bright blue/yellow/orange palette. Realistic eyes gave an uncanny-valley effect, so I abstracted the faces into featureless silhouettes — which read cleaner at thumbnail size and turned the hosts into a scalable, iconic mark rather than standard portraiture.

The face-card concept won the competition, and the client retained me to build it into a full broadcast package — lower thirds, animated title cards, and YouTube banners, all built on the same modular artwork. The identity is still in active use on the show today.
